property_summary: For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true only if interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, but not for other interface IDs (like IERC165).
The function supportsInterface(bytes4) must return true for the IERC165 interface ID.
supportsInterface(IERC165) returns true in the reference contract but false in the mutant.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true for IERC165 interface ID.
supportInterface(IERC165.interfaceId) returns true for all valid fuzz inputs leading to a cancel call.
For any bytes4 interface ID, supportsInterface returns true for both IAccessControl and IERC165 on the reference, but returns false for IAccessControl on the mutant.
The supportsInterface function always returns true for the IAccessControl interface ID.
After any cancel call, supportsInterface returns true for the IAccessControl interface ID.
After any sequence of public calls ending with cancel, the contract always reports support for the IAccessControl interface.
After any cancel call reverts as expected, supportsInterface still returns true for IAccessControl.
For any interface ID, supportsInterface should match the reference behavior for IAccessControl and IERC165.
The supportsInterface function returns false for interface ID 0xffffffff in the reference contract.
The supportsInterface function returns true for interface ID type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId, not for 0xffffffff.
For the cancel function, calling supportsInterface with any interfaceId should return only true for IAccessControl or IERC165 interface IDs, not for 0xffffffff.
The supportsInterface function returns false for any interfaceId that is not the IAccessControl or IERC165 interface IDs.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, if supportsInterface returns true, then it must also return true for the inverse of that interfaceId (i.e., for the same query).
For any address account, if the contract has role bytes32(0) on account, then it has role bytes32(0) on address(this)
supportsInterface reflection: For any bytes4 interfaceId, calling supportsInterface on the contract itself returns consistent results across two consecutive calls.
Calling supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns the same boolean value when called from address(this) and from any other account.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true if and only if it also returns true for the same interfaceId when queried through the public getter.
For any interface id, supportsInterface returns true for IAccessControl's interface id or false otherwise.
supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns exactly true for interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId and returns super.supportsInterface(interfaceId) otherwise.
After canceling a scheduled operation, the operation's timestamp reverts to 0, which is not equal to _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1) before scheduling.
For any interface ID, supportsInterface returns exactly interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or super.supportsInterface(interfaceId).
For any interfaceId, calling supportsInterface twice in succession returns the same value.
For any address, calling supportsInterface(bytes4) on the TimelockController (C) returns the same value as on the underlying AccessControl contract (via the public getter).
Calling supportsInterface with type(IAccessControl).interfaceId returns true and with other valid interface IDs follows the ERC165 specification.
The supportsInterface function returns true for the IAccessControl interface ID.
Calling supportsInterface with the interface ID of IERC165 returns true.
For any bytes4 interface ID, the supportsInterface function returns true if and only if it equals the IAccessControl interface ID.
For any operation id, if it is pending then it cannot be cancelled after it is ready.
If an operation id is not pending, then it must also not be cancellable.
Cancelling a non-pending operation should always revert.
After a successful cancel, the operation id is no longer pending.
For any operation id, if it is not pending then cancel must revert.
The getRoleAdmin function should return the stored admin role for a given role, not always the default admin role.
The return value of getRoleAdmin for the same role must be consistent before and after cancel is called on a pending operation.
The admin role of a role must equal the stored admin role, which can differ from DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE.
getRoleAdmin returns the stored admin role for a given role, which may differ from DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE.
The admin role of a role should be equal to the admin role returned by getRoleAdmin, which is the stored admin role and can differ from DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE.
For any bytes32 role, getRoleAdmin returns the keccak256 hash of the role string combined with the admin role marker.
getRoleAdmin returns the adminRole stored for that role when invoked before cancel sets it as TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE.
getRoleAdmin returns the adminRole stored for that role after cancel sets it as TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE.
For any bytes32 role, getRoleAdmin(role) returns the same value regardless of whether cancel was called on the same operation id multiple times.
getRoleAdmin returns the admin role that was set via _setRoleAdmin, not a hash of the role itself.
For any role, getRoleAdmin returns the same value as the role itself when the role is its own admin.
For the admin role (0x00), cancel reverts when called by a non-admin account.
For any role, getRoleAdmin returns the admin role that was set via _setRoleAdmin.
For any role that is not its own admin, getRoleAdmin returns a value different from the role itself.
The role admin of a role set as its own admin remains the same role after any role operation.
getRoleAdmin returns the admin role of a given role, not the role itself
cancel(bytes32) should only be callable by an account with the proposer role, whose admin is the timelock admin role.
After cancel, the operation timestamp is deleted, so the operation should not be pending.
grantRole and revokeRole check the admin role of the role, not the role itself.
cancel() only succeeds when the caller has the proposer role, which is only granted to the deployer (address(this)) and not to arbitrary accounts.
After calling cancel on an operation that has been scheduled, the operation's timestamp should become zero (i.e., it should no longer be pending or ready).
After a cancel operation, the caller can still renounce their own role.
After cancel, the caller who is a PROPOSER can still renounce their own PROPOSER role.
After cancel, the contract's renounceRole function still works for the caller who is a proposer.
After canceling an operation, a proposer can successfully renounce their own PROPOSER_ROLE.
The isOperation function returns true for any bytes32 id only if the timestamp is strictly greater than 0.
cancel should only succeed when isOperationPending returns true for the operation id.
For any bytes32 id, calling cancel(id) should revert if isOperation(id) returns false.
For any bytes32 id, cancel(id) reverts when getTimestamp(id) is 0
For any bytes32 id, cancel(id) reverts when getTimestamp(id) equals 0.
isOperation returns true for any operation that was previously scheduled and not yet executed (i.e., cancel should only succeed for pending operations).
The return value of isOperation for an arbitrary operation id changes after calling cancel with that id.
After cancel, isOperation returns false for the canceled operation ID.
Calling cancel with an operation id that was never scheduled always reverts.
The cancel function should only revert when called with a non-pending operation, and isOperation returns true exactly when the operation has been scheduled and not yet executed.
After calling cancel with a non-pending operation id, isOperation should return false for that id.
When calling cancel with a non-pending operation id, the operation should not be marked as pending after cancellation.
After calling cancel with an operation id that is not pending, the operation remains not pending (i.e., isOperationPending returns false).
After calling cancel with an operation id that is not pending, isOperationPending returns false for that id.
Calling cancel on an operation that is currently pending should revert.
After scheduling an operation with delay=0, the operation should be pending regardless of when cancel is called.
A newly scheduled operation with delay 0 is pending immediately after scheduling.
An operation scheduled with delay=0 is pending before and after cancel reverts.
An operation that is not done and has a timestamp > 1 can be cancelled, with isOperationPending returning true just before cancel.

After scheduling an operation with delay=0 and then canceling it, the operation is not done (isOperationDone returns false) and its timestamp is 0, meaning it was pending before cancel and not pending after cancel.
For any operation id, if isOperationPending(id) is true after scheduling, it must remain true until the operation is executed or cancelled.
If isOperationPending(id) returns false, then calling cancel(id) must revert.
If isOperationPending(id) returns false, then the timestamp for that id must be exactly DONE_TIMESTAMP (1), not 0.
For any operation id, if isOperationPending(id) returns false and getTimestamp(id) is NOT equal to DONE_TIMESTAMP (1), then cancel(id) must revert.
If getTimestamp(id) returns 0, then isOperationPending(id) must return false.
After scheduling an operation, it cannot be canceled until the operation is pending (i.e., its timestamp > _DONE_TIMESTAMP). Canceling an operation that is not pending should revert.
An operation that is not pending (i.e., not yet scheduled or already completed) cannot be cancelled.
If no operation is pending for a given id, isOperationDone(id) should return true.
After an operation's timestamp is set to positive (i.e., scheduled), cancel must revert unless the operation is pending (timestamp > _DONE_TIMESTAMP).
After an operation is cancelled, isOperationDone should return true and subsequent cancel should revert.
For any operation id, isOperationDone returns true if and only if the operation timestamp equals 1.
For any operation that is not scheduled, isOperationDone returns false.
If an operation is scheduled and pending, then calling cancel should make it not pending, and cancel should revert if called a second time.
For any operation id, if isOperationDone returns true, then isOperationPending must return false.
For any operation id, isOperationDone returns false when getTimestamp returns a value greater than 1.
For any operation id, if cancel(id) reverts then the operation must have been pending after its scheduling; but after cancel(id) succeeds, isOperationPending(id) must return false.
After a successful cancel(id), isOperationPending(id) must return false.
If cancel(id) succeeds, then isOperationPending(id) must return false.
After a successful cancel(id), getTimestamp(id) must return 1 (DONE_TIMESTAMP) or 0 (not pending), but not a value greater than 0 that indicates pending.
After a successful cancel(id), the operation still appears pending (isOperationPending returns true) if getTimestamp returns 0 instead of 1.

For all operations that are not the zero operation (hash != 0) and have been scheduled with a delay, calling cancel on them before the delay passes will successfully cancel the operation, i.e., the timestamp for the operation becomes 0.
The getMinDelay function always returns a non-zero value after the first updateDelay call sets a positive delay.
The getMinDelay function returns the same value before and after any cancel call that does not revert.
For a proposed operation that is not yet executed, calling getMinDelay before and after scheduling the operation with the same delay returns the same value.
The getMinDelay function always returns the same value before and after a successful cancel operation on a pending operation.
